statement: The first line holds n; each of the next n lines holds an interval as two integers l and r. Merge every pair of overlapping or touching intervals and print the result, one merged interval per line as l and r separated by a space, sorted by left end. Sort the intervals by l and sweep: keep a current interval, extend its right end while the next interval starts at or before it, and emit it when a gap appears. Touching intervals - one ends where the next begins - merge into one.

example.why: 1-3 and 2-6 overlap and fuse into 1-6; the other two stand apart.

hint: After sorting, a single comparison per interval decides: extend the current one, or emit and restart.
mistake: Extending with the new right end unconditionally - a contained interval like 2-4 inside 1-6 must shrink nothing.
